newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Laying off OTC risk in Telebras.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Laying off OTC risk in Telebras.

text.p: Institutions were selling November and December calls on Telecomunicacoes Brasileiras SA (Telebras) and buying longer dated puts, possibly to hedge an over-the-counter (OTC) trade, traders said Friday.
The Telebras November 75 call traded a total of 845 contracts and the December 75 call traded 4,300. The January 70 puts traded 900 contracts and the April 70 put traded 500.
Telebras options trade on the American Stock Exchange, the Chicago Board Options Exchange, the Philadelphia Stock Exchange and the New York Stock Exchange.
At 1050 CDT (1550 GMT), Telebras shares in the U.S. were down 3/8 at 74-1/4, off their 73-7/8 intraday low. Consolidated volume totalled 811,500 shares.
"It appears put buyers are buying long term and institutions are selling the November and December calls," said a trader in Chicago.
He said there was no news on the Brazil state telecommunications company that was influencing the trading.

On Wednesday, a Brazilian court ruled that a 1990 subscription offer by Telebras was valid, meaning the company could be forced to issue 13.7 billion new shares if the government loses an appeal in a higher court.
Telebras shares fell sharply earlier this week ahead of and just after the court's ruling.
The stock rose to 81-1/2 intraday Monday before closing at 80-1/8. Its intraday low of 73-7/8 Friday was the stock's lowest point since early September.
The drop in the share price also affected the options premiums, mostly on the call side.

A week ago, for instance, the November 75 calls were trading around 6-1/2. On Friday, trades in that option crossed at 1-7/8. The premium on the December 75 calls was around eight early this week but fell to the 3-1/2 area by Friday.
The movement in premiums on the active puts was less dramatic, as the January 70 put went from about 1-1/2 at the beginning of the week to 2-11/16 Friday.
